name: MonarchAiConversation
title: useAiConversation
wrapsNative: Observation (@Observable, on the main actor) over an injected transport that returns AsyncThrowingStream; Codable for the message model
summary: Headless state for an AI conversation: it sends prompts through an injected transport, streams the reply into the vendor-neutral message model, and handles stop, regenerate, retry, edit and resend as branches, tool approval, client-side tools, an offline queue and feedback.
whenToUse: As the model behind any chat surface. Keep it in @State or in your own model, read messages, status and error in views, and implement MonarchAiTransport for your backend.
whenNotToUse: Not for a single completion in a text field, which is MonarchAiCompletion with AiGhostText. It draws nothing: use the AI components to show the messages.
api: init(transport: any MonarchAiTransport, initialMessages: [MonarchAiConversationMessage] = [], conversationId: String? = nil, body: [String: MonarchAiJSON] = [:], queuesWhileOffline: Bool = true, slowAfter: Duration? = .seconds(10), connectionLostMessage: String? = nil, toolResultFailedMessage: String? = nil, generateId: (@MainActor () -> String)? = nil)
@discardableResult func send(_ text: String, files: [MonarchAiFilePart] = [], body: [String: MonarchAiJSON] = [:]) -> Bool
func regenerate(_ messageId: String? = nil, body: [String: MonarchAiJSON] = [:])
func retry(_ messageId: String? = nil, body: [String: MonarchAiJSON] = [:])
func editAndResend(_ messageId: String, text: String, files: [MonarchAiFilePart]? = nil, body: [String: MonarchAiJSON] = [:])
func approveTool(_ toolCallId: String, input: MonarchAiJSON? = nil)
func denyTool(_ toolCallId: String, reason: String? = nil)
func submitToolResult(_ toolCallId: String, _ result: MonarchAiToolResult)
func branchTo(_ messageId: String, index: Int)
func setFeedback(_ messageId: String, _ feedback: MonarchAiMessageFeedback?)

protocol MonarchAiTransport: Sendable { func stream(_ request: MonarchAiTransportRequest) -> MonarchAiEventStream; var respondsToTools: Bool { get }; func respondToTool(_ response: MonarchAiToolResponse) -> MonarchAiEventStream; var resumesRuns: Bool { get }; func resume(_ request: MonarchAiResumeRequest) -> MonarchAiEventStream }
enum MonarchAiStreamEvent { case agent, textDelta, reasoningDelta, reasoningEnd, part, toolUpdate, toolInputDelta, finish, run, usage, memory, done, error }

struct MonarchAiConversationMessage: Identifiable, Sendable, Hashable, Codable { id, role, parts, agent, createdAt, model, usage, feedback, branch, finishReason, runId, isQueued; var text: String; var isStreaming: Bool; var toolCalls: [MonarchAiToolCallPart]; var memories: [MonarchAiMemoryPart]; var createdDate: Date?; static func timestamp(_ date: Date) -> String }
enum MonarchAiPart: Sendable, Hashable, Codable { case text, reasoning, toolCall, citation, source, file, artifact, editProposal, plan, ui, memory, error; var type: String }

Part and value types: MonarchAiTextPart, MonarchAiReasoningPart, MonarchAiToolCallPart, MonarchAiCitationPart, MonarchAiSourcePart, MonarchAiFilePart, MonarchAiArtifactPart, MonarchAiEditProposalPart, MonarchAiPlanPart, MonarchAiPlanStep, MonarchAiUiPart, MonarchAiMemoryPart, MonarchAiErrorPart, MonarchAiUsage, MonarchAiAgentRef, MonarchAiBranchPosition, MonarchAiJSON

Enumerations: MonarchAiRole, MonarchAiPartState, MonarchAiToolCallState, MonarchAiToolCallRisk, MonarchAiFinishReason, MonarchAiSourceKind, MonarchAiArtifactKind, MonarchAiEditProposalState, MonarchAiPlanStepState, MonarchAiMemoryAction, MonarchAiMessageFeedback, MonarchAiTrigger, MonarchAiConversationStatus, MonarchAiToolDecision, MonarchAiToolResult

Requests and results: MonarchAiTransportRequest, MonarchAiToolResponse, MonarchAiResumeRequest, MonarchAiToolCallPatch, MonarchAiQueuedMessage, MonarchAiConversationError (static func isRetryable(code: String?) -> Bool)

options.name: transport
options.description: Connects the conversation to your backend. Monarch does no networking.

options.name: initialMessages
options.description: Messages to start with, for example a stored conversation. Shown as one branch.

options.name: conversationId
options.description: The id from an earlier session, sent with every request. A done event replaces it.

options.name: body
options.description: Request fields sent on every turn, merged under the fields given to send. Also a settable property.

options.name: queuesWhileOffline
options.description: While offline, send keeps the message in queued and sends it, in order, once setOnline(true) is called.

options.name: slowAfter
options.description: The time without any event from a running reply before isSlow becomes true. nil turns it off.

options.name: connectionLostMessage
options.description: Replaces the built-in "The connection was lost." of the error raised when the stream throws.

options.name: toolResultFailedMessage
options.description: Replaces the built-in "The tool result could not be sent." recorded when a client-side tool throws without a message.

options.name: generateId
options.description: Custom message ids. The default is a UUID.

states.name: submitted
states.description: Sent, waiting for the first event. isBusy is true.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Events are arriving and messages changes with each one. isBusy is true.

states.name: awaitingApproval
states.description: A tool call waits for approveTool or denyTool. canSend is false and send returns false.

states.name: awaitingToolResult
states.description: The model called a tool the client runs: onToolCall runs it, or call submitToolResult.

states.name: error
states.description: The last turn failed. error holds the code, the message and whether it can be retried or resumed; the reply ends with an error part.

states.name: stopped
states.description: stop() ended the reply. What arrived stays, streaming parts are closed and running tool calls are cancelled.

states.name: offline
states.description: After setOnline(false), sent messages wait in queued and appear at the end of messages with isQueued.

states.name: slow
states.description: isSlow is true while a running reply has sent nothing for slowAfter.

appearance: None: it is a model and draws nothing.
platformNotes: The web is the useAiConversation hook; here it is an @Observable class. The message model has the web's fields and reads and writes the web's JSON (kebab-case raw values, a type field per part); the model type is MonarchAiConversationMessage because MonarchAiMessage is the message view. Times stay ISO 8601 strings, with createdDate and timestamp(_:) for Date. Fields the web types as unknown are MonarchAiJSON. Not offered, because they belong to the browser or to a transport: File uploads (uploadFile, inlineFiles, uploads, onUploadProgress; send takes file parts the app has already uploaded), the SSE, provider, AG-UI and Rook transports and their mappers, the testing kit, and submit as a promise (send returns whether the message was accepted). There is no AbortSignal: the stream is read in a task that is cancelled on stop. The network source is setOnline(_:), fed by the app, for example from NWPathMonitor. Updates are not batched per frame; SwiftUI coalesces observation changes itself. With a tool policy, every waiting call is put to the policy before the status is decided; the web stops at the first decided call.
accessibility: It draws nothing and announces nothing; the components that show the messages do.
isSlow, isQueued, the error message and the tool call states are plain values, so a view can speak them.
edgeCases: Sending while a reply streams ends that reply, keeping what arrived, and starts the next.
A done or error event ends the reply even if the transport keeps the stream open; a stream that ends without done leaves the status idle and does not call onFinish.
A stream that throws ends the reply with the retryable code network. With a run id and a transport that resumes runs, the error is resumable.
retry rewrites the same message; regenerate and editAndResend add a branch, and messages then carry branch with the index and count.
A queued message that fails holds the rest of the queue until the connection comes back again.
Sending a new message cancels tool calls that still waited for a client-side result.
Releasing the conversation cancels the task that reads the stream.
Decoding a part with an unknown type throws.

A stored conversation, read from the web's JSON
examples.setup:
private let stored: [MonarchAiConversationMessage] = {
    let json = """
        [{"id": "u1", "role": "user", "createdAt": "2025-03-10T12:00:00.000Z",
          "parts": [{"type": "text", "text": "Hello", "state": "done"}]}]
        """
    return (try? JSONDecoder().decode([MonarchAiConversationMessage].self, from: Data(json.utf8))) ?? []
}()
